newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS upgrades Nova Scotia's short-term ratings.
newsitem.headline: DBRS upgrades Nova Scotia's short-term ratings.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service said on Wednesday it upgraded the short-term ratings of Nova Scotia to R-1 (low) from R-2 (high) with a stable trend.
The Toronto-based bond rating agency maintained the Atlantic province's long-term rating at BBB (high) with a stable trend.
The improved short-term rating, which applies to both the province's debt and debt guaranteed by the province, reflects the signifcant improvement in the Nova Scotia's fiscal performance, DBRS said.
The province's short-term level has returned to the level it was at before 1993. The agency noted that Nova Scotia has moved from a sizable deficit in fiscal 1992-93 to a surplus in 1996-97.

DBRS said it remains concerned with the small size of the province's surpluses relative to potential volatility from its large exposure to foreign exchange risk on its outstanding direct debt. However, the agency noted the province has implemented targets and policy to reduce this risk.

Current sluggish economic conditions and a still significant level of debt precludes an improvement in Nova Scotia's long-term rating, DBRS said. Nova Scotia's debt to GDP is the third highest of the Canadian provinces and growth rates remain well below national averages.
